title: Simple RPG Battle
story: A hero with 100 HP faces a dragon with 150 HP. The hero can attack (deal 15-25 damage) or heal (recover 10-20 HP) — but healing wastes a turn the dragon uses to attack. Every decision matters. Build the battle system that powers every RPG.
why: An RPG battle system combines structs for characters, enums for actions, random damage ranges, and turn-based logic — the core of combat in any role-playing game.
analogy: A boxing match: two fighters trading blows, each punch dealing variable damage. Between rounds, a fighter might rest (heal). Your RPG battle is the referee counting HP instead of punches — when someone hits zero, the other hand is raised in victory.
try_it: Add critical hits (10% chance, 2x damage). Add a special attack that deals extra damage but has a cooldown. Add defense stat that reduces incoming damage. Implement player choice: each turn, choose 'attack' or 'heal'. Add status effects: poison (damage over time), stun (skip turn).
tips: Clamp HP between 0 and max_hp — prevents negative HP or overhealing
Check death after every attack — don't let dead characters keep fighting
common_mistakes: Not checking for death immediately after damage — zombie character continues fighting
Overhealing without clamping — HP exceeds max, breaking game balance
Using the same seed for both characters — they deal identical damage patterns
